summary.headline: GPT Infra FY26 consolidated revenue rose 8.6% to INR1,290 crores, below guidance, while consolidated EBITDA grew 28.5% to INR174.2 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 1.3% YoY to INR373.9 crores, while consolidated revenue grew 8.9% to INR414.7 crores; management attributed the March shortfall to West Bengal elections and labour migration. Margins improved, with standalone Q4 EBITDA up 27% to INR53 crores at 14% margin and consolidated Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR59.2 crores, helped by the Ghana factory. The Alcon signalling EPC acquisition (INR151.83 crores cash) closed in the quarter and is being merged into GPT Infra with an appointed date of April 1, 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 27-30%, order inflow of about INR3,000 crores and consolidated EBITDA margin of around 14%.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Contributed more than 90% of FY26 revenue; key executing projects include Prayagraj Ganga Bridge, Kona Expressway and Raniganj. Alcon signalling will be reported within the infra line item.

segments.name: Concrete sleepers
segments.commentary: Management said the segment was profitable in FY26 on domestic demand and African operations. Q4 was loss-making in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, which management attributed mainly to currency mark-to-market effects; Ghana production has started.

segments.name: Signalling (Alcon, acquired)
segments.commentary: Margin of about 20% vs 13-14% for traditional infra; FY27 revenue expected at INR120-130 crores. Order book is about INR90-100 crores; FY27 order inflow expected at INR150-200 crores against about INR500 crores of bids.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%, subject to Middle East war-related economic headwinds; long-term revenue growth target above 20%.
FY27 order inflow guidance of about INR3,000 crores across infra, signalling and sleepers.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 14% for FY27, with long-term standalone and consolidated margin above 13%.
West Bengal catch-up expected: April subdued again due to elections, Q1 not fully caught up, but first half expected to recover the shortfall.
Average capex of about INR70-75 crores a year for the next couple of years including the HAM equity share of INR55-60 crores; equipment purchases of INR40-50 crores a year.
Alcon and GPT merger (appointed date April 1, 2026) expected to complete in FY27, subject to regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Acquired Alcon Builders and Engineers (New Delhi EPC signalling) for INR151.83 crores cash; wholly owned subsidiary from January 1, 2026.
First HAM contract (elevated bypass, Jodhpur, NHAI), contract value about INR669 crores; GPT holds 51% in the SPV, which is already incorporated.
Steel girder fabrication factory at Singur, West Bengal, started during the year with about 10,000 tonnes per annum capacity; further expansion under review.
Ghana facility commercially operational, with first supply and invoice raised in March 2026.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of INR2,422 crores in FY26, and about INR500 crores of Alcon signalling bids in the last two months; Alcon contracts of INR70-80 crores individually.

Major wins: Northern Railway rail-cum-road bridge over Ganga at Varanasi, INR1,201 crores total (GPT share 40%, about INR481 crores); MCGM LBS Marg flyover, INR1,805 crores total (JV share 26%, about INR470 crores).
Price escalation formulas in all contracts, linked to SAIL/RINL steel, WPI for cement and fuel; NHAI and MoRTH moved to monthly escalation payments and allowed a 4-month force majeure extension.
Management said about 40% of revenue comes from West Bengal, and migrant labour returning from there was disrupted in March and April.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract assets rise from INR336 crores to about INR514 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60-65 crores is from Alcon (retention, unbilled revenue, escalation), with the rest from EPC milestone-based billing; contract assets are typically 6-8 months old and are targeted to fall to 3-4 months of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the QIP proceeds go, given limited debt reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt was cut by about INR125-130 crores from March 2024 to March 2025; FY26 debt rose on EPC working-capital drawdowns and internal accruals used for the Alcon purchase, with debt expected to return to the earlier level.

qa_highlights.question: Did West Bengal elections cause the revenue guidance miss, and does Alcon's INR140 crores contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed March execution was hit by elections and labour migration; the Alcon contribution in FY26 was only Q4 numbers of about INR30 crores, since it was consolidated from January 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is labour back and is there execution risk to FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: April was again subdued by elections, but May execution is strong and labour is back on site; new contracts won in December and January are expected to contribute heavily in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation from the war affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carry escalation formulas; NHAI now pays escalation monthly, so a lag is possible, but management expects full-year margins to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and is Alcon consolidated separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Average capex about INR70-75 crores a year including the HAM share; Alcon is consolidated and, after the merger, will report within the infra segment rather than as a separate line.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 27-30% in FY27 depends on recovering the March and April shortfall in the first half; April was subdued again by elections.
Middle East war effects on metal and fuel prices, currency and government payment timing; escalation may lag by a month.

Contract assets at about INR514 crores (consolidated) and debt increase in FY26 against the QIP deconsolidation narrative; working-capital conversion of 75-80% of contract assets in H1 FY27 is targeted.
Concrete sleeper segment losses in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, driven by currency volatility.
Signalling order inflow of INR150-200 crores in FY27 against the INR500 crores of bids; execution of the Alcon merger subject to regulatory approvals.
Q4 revenue was 40% H2-weighted seasonality; management said it cannot be removed from the business.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth, margins and order inflow, with a clear explanation of the election-related shortfall. Management was more guarded when asked about faster growth, citing the Middle East war and reliance on government payments. Answers on debt reduction and contract-asset build-up were thinner and deferred to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: We are confident of achieving a long-term growth in the -- in revenue in excess of 20%, with revenue this year expected to cross 27% to 30% for the year, subject to the headwinds with respect to the economic conditions on account of the war in the Middle East.
The signaling business has a margin profile of almost 20% compared to the 13% / 14% for the traditional infra business that we were doing.
So we don't anticipate much of a -- so a lot of these contracts that you're referring to INR2,400-odd crores are contracts that we have received in the last financial year.
